solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Piece of mathematics old geometers worked out — hard to penetrate it

indicators.note: one piece must go into the other, here H pushing inside the reworked letters ('it')
letters that are worked out are solved like a puzzle and rearranged into new order

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone says a famous mathematical result was devised by old geometers and is hard to grasp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out' rearranges OLDGEOMETERS into GODELSTEOREM; 'to penetrate it' puts H inside that, 'it' standing for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Gödel's incompleteness theorem is a celebrated result of mathematical logic, so it is literally a piece of mathematics.

clue.text: A university peters out after good reunions

indicators.note: the letters for the remainder of the clue follow the single letter for good

parts.note: to peter out is to fade away, to die

explanation.surface: A college's alumni gatherings dwindle away.
explanation.walkthrough: A gaudy is a feast or reunion held for former members at an Oxford or Cambridge college.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaudies are celebratory college dinners for returning graduates, so they are gatherings of old members.

clue.text: Me? I'd stop awful tyranny

indicators.note: something awful is in a dreadful state, so these letters are jumbled into another order

parts.note: the words themselves are the fodder to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A would-be autocrat vows to halt dreadful oppression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges ME I'D STOP, but that gives only eight letters with one S; the answer needs two, so the setter's fodder is a letter short.
explanation.definitionFit: Despotism is absolute rule by one person, a synonym for tyranny.

clue.text: Overweight woman eating last bit of hamburger

indicators.note: the word for woman takes in another letter as if consuming it

parts.note: a lady is a woman

indicators.note: only the final letter of hamburger is used

explanation.surface: A fat woman tucks into a burger.
explanation.definitionFit: Lardy is informal for fat, plump, carrying too much weight.

clue.text: Cheaper and nastier item for wiping marble?

parts.note: a taw is a playing marble, especially the shooter
a drier, such as a cloth, is something used to wipe things dry

explanation.surface: A question about a cloth for polishing marble, set beside cheap and nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, a 'taw drier' is a thing for drying a marble, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Tawdry means showy but cheap and of poor quality, so the comparative is cheaper and nastier.

clue.text: Get rid of very loud star after end of performance

indicators.note: only the final letter of performance is wanted

parts.note: FF is fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud
an ace is a star performer

explanation.surface: A theatrical instruction to dismiss a loud star once the show ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To efface is to erase or wipe out, so to remove entirely.

clue.text: Children (apart from one of them) on the uphill path, getting new vitality

indicators.note: signals that the word for one of the children is taken away from the plural

parts.note: one of the children is a child
an ascent is a path climbing upwards

explanation.surface: Youngsters heading uphill find renewed energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apart from one of them' removes CHILD from CHILDREN, leaving REN; 'on' simply joins it to ASCENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Renascent means being reborn or reviving, hence acquiring fresh vigour.

clue.text: African mothers, tip-top

parts.note: ma is mother, so mas are mothers
A1 or AI means first-rate, tip-top

explanation.surface: Mothers in Africa praised as excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masai are a people of Kenya and Tanzania, so one of them is an African.

clue.text: Less productive student deficient in one of the R's

indicators.note: lacking something, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: a learner is a student
the three R's are reading, writing and arithmetic; their initial R is removed

explanation.surface: A weaker pupil lacking skill in reading, writing or arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Lean years are thin, unproductive ones, so leaner means yielding less.

clue.text: International organisation's team is loose (going round in circles)

parts.note: the UN is the United Nations, plus the possessive S
a crew is a team

explanation.surface: A United Nations team is running wild, aimlessly circling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' is a verb here, to unfasten, and the bracket says how: by turning.
explanation.definitionFit: To unscrew a fitting is to free it by rotating it repeatedly.

clue.text: Adroitness of female actually existing

parts.note: in esse is Latin for in actual existence

explanation.surface: The skill of a woman who really exists.
explanation.definitionFit: Finesse is delicate skill or subtlety in handling things, a synonym for dexterity.

clue.text: Girl collecting gold and hard white stuff

indicators.note: the girl's name gathers up another piece inside itself

parts.note: Ivy is a girl's name
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A girl gathers gold and a hard white substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephant tusks are made of this hard creamy-white dentine.

clue.text: So sincere about a big financial problem

indicators.note: the letters are moved about into another order

explanation.surface: Someone genuinely worried about a major economic difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: An economic downturn of falling output is a serious monetary problem for a country.

clue.text: Good person feels irritation — result of surgical treatment?

parts.note: ST is saint, a good person
something that itches feels irritated

explanation.surface: A kindly patient finds the wound itching after an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Sutures closing an incision are what an operation commonly leaves behind.

clue.text: This writer has inaccurate article about friar

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the setter's pronoun
inaccurate letters are wrongly placed, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A writer admits a faulty article about a monk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This writer' is the setter speaking of himself, a standard way to clue ME; 'has' merely joins it to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A Carmelite is a member of the Order of Our Lady of Mount Carmel, a mendicant religious order.

clue.text: Moderate anger

definitions.meaning: a fit of rage, as in losing one's cool

explanation.surface: Keep your rage in check.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb meaning tone down and a noun meaning a bad mood.

clue.text: Star with external power and endless cash, the means to attract a mate?

definitions.text: the means to attract a mate?

indicators.note: the other pieces sit on the outside, surrounding the word for star

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for cash is dropped

parts.note: money is cash
a hero is a star

explanation.surface: A rich, powerful celebrity using fame to woo a partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' turns MONEY into MONE; P and MONE go on either side of HERO.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals secrete chemical signals to draw in sexual partners; that is the question-marked sense.

clue.text: Greek writer's place linked with tree

indicators.note: the two words are interlocked like chain links rather than set side by side, so their letters mix

parts.note: to put something is to place it
the larch is a deciduous conifer

explanation.surface: A Greek author's home is associated with a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words are not simply joined: they interlock like chain links, the first letter of the tree sitting inside the word for place. The 's after the definition is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Plutarch was the Greek biographer and essayist who wrote the Parallel Lives.

clue.text: Quality of wood that is a bit twisted at one end

indicators.text: a bit twisted at one end
indicators.note: only the last two letters of the word for wood are turned round

parts.note: timber is wood

explanation.surface: The grain of a piece of wood is warped at one end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit twisted at one end' swaps the final ER of TIMBER to RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbre is the tone quality or colour of a sound, as distinct from its pitch.

clue.text: Little 'un eats 'uge pile — sitter on kitchen table too!

indicators.note: the child's word takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: a tot is a small child
with the H dropped, as in the clue's accent, heap becomes 'eap

explanation.surface: A toddler wolfs a huge helping while sitting on the table too.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped aitches signal that HEAP loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: The pot for brewing tea typically stands on a kitchen table, so it sits there.

clue.text: Lifeless principal is a fishy type

parts.note: flat means dull, lifeless
a head is a principal, as of a school

explanation.surface: A dull headteacher is a suspicious character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fishy' looks like 'dubious' but means a kind of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatheads are a family of bottom-dwelling fish with flattened skulls.

clue.text: Puts down D, D, … when test is held

indicators.note: the test is held inside the spelled-out letters

parts.note: several Ds, the letter written as a word, are dees
the MOT is the annual UK roadworthiness test for vehicles

explanation.surface: Lowering grades to D when an exam is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: To demote someone is to lower them in rank, to put them down a level.

clue.text: Scoundrel that's hard on the outside and nasty inside?

definitions.text: that's hard on the outside and nasty inside?
definitions.meaning: describes a rotten shelled breakfast item: a hard shell outside, putrid within

explanation.surface: A villain tough-seeming yet rotten at heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotter is called this idiomatically, and literally it is a spoiled egg with its hard shell.

clue.text: What may be on smartphone — pictures etc showing food

parts.note: an applet is a small application program found on a phone
art covers pictures and the like

explanation.surface: Photos of a meal displayed on a phone screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastry dessert filled with fruit is a dish, so a kind of food.

clue.text: Ways to show sadness but not love

indicators.note: excluding something, so a letter is removed

parts.note: pathos is a quality evoking sadness
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Methods of expressing grief without affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Paths are routes or courses, the same as ways.

clue.text: Brush could alternatively be shrub

definitions.meaning: a yellow-flowered leguminous bush of heathland

explanation.surface: A brush might equally be a bush.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a sweeping implement and the gorse-like plant whose twigs once made them.

clue.text: Get something to chew as you might say indeed!

indicators.note: signals that the words are pronounced, giving a soundalike

parts.note: to buy gum is to get something to chew

explanation.surface: An exclamation while picking up chewing gum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By gum!' is a mild exclamation associated with northern England, a euphemism for 'by God'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exclamation of emphasis or surprise, like saying 'my word!'.

clue.text: Away team no longer in the changing room?

definitions.text: no longer in the changing room?

parts.note: out means away, as in 'out of the office'
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A visiting team has left the dressing room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Away' looks like the definition of the whole answer but only gives OUT; the question-marked tail is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Players who have left the dressing room are out of doors, on the pitch in the open air.

clue.text: See weed grow out of control — rodent will eat it

indicators.note: the rodent takes the jumbled letters inside

parts.note: a rat is a rodent

indicators.note: letters running wild are rearranged

explanation.surface: Watch a weed spread wildly, with a rat feeding on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' has no wordplay role; it only makes the surface a sentence, leaving the definition 'weed' mid-clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragwort is a yellow-flowered plant, toxic to livestock, regarded as an invasive weed.

clue.text: Drivers into the ground make offensive comments to Upton Park players

parts.note: in cricket, to sledge is to taunt an opponent verbally
West Ham United, long based at Upton Park in London, are nicknamed the Hammers

explanation.surface: Insulting West Ham footballers.
explanation.walkthrough: Upton Park was West Ham United's London football ground; sledging is cricket slang for taunting.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy long-handled hammers are used for driving stakes or posts into the earth.
